knownDifferences.name: string.equality.ref
knownDifferences.code: { var a = "ab"; var b = string.Concat("a", "b"); return B(a == b) + "," + B((object)a == (object)b) + "," + B(a.Equals(b)); }
knownDifferences.difference: JavaScript strings are values: two equal strings are never different references.

knownDifferences.name: boxing.equality
knownDifferences.code: { object a = 1, b = 1; return B(a == b) + "," + B(a.Equals(b)) + "," + B(Equals(a, b)); }
knownDifferences.difference: Values are not boxed in JavaScript: two boxed equal numbers compare equal by reference too.
knownDifferences.alternative: Compare unboxed values instead of relying on reference identity.

knownDifferences.name: float.precision
knownDifferences.difference: `float` is a JavaScript number, so it keeps double precision instead of rounding to single.
knownDifferences.alternative: Use `double`, or a Float32Array from WebSharper.JavaScript when single-precision storage matters.

knownDifferences.name: array.outofrange
knownDifferences.difference: Array accesses are not bounds-checked: reading past the end gives undefined instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.

knownDifferences.name: exception.null.deref
knownDifferences.difference: Dereferencing null throws a JavaScript TypeError, not a NullReferenceException.
knownDifferences.alternative: Check for null (or use ?.) instead of catching NullReferenceException.

knownDifferences.name: dict.insertion.order
knownDifferences.code: { var d = new Dictionary<string, int> { ["b"] = 1, ["a"] = 2, ["c"] = 3 }; d.Remove("a"); d["d"] = 4; return J(d.Keys); }
knownDifferences.difference: After a Remove, .NET reuses the freed slot for the next Add; that order is unspecified in .NET, and JavaScript keeps insertion order.
knownDifferences.alternative: Sort the keys, or use SortedDictionary, when order matters.

knownDifferences.name: generic.default
knownDifferences.difference: Generics are erased: default(T) inside generic code is null for value types too.
knownDifferences.alternative: Pass the default value in, or constrain T to a class.

knownDifferences.name: enum.getvalues
knownDifferences.difference: Enums are erased to numbers: a boxed or generic enum value formats as its number.
knownDifferences.alternative: Call ToString on the statically typed enum value.

knownDifferences.name: list.capacity.tostring
knownDifferences.difference: No runtime type names: Object.ToString on a type that does not override it does not give the .NET type name.

knownDifferences.name: object.tostring.default
knownDifferences.difference: No runtime type names: Object.ToString on a type that does not override it does not give the .NET type name.

knownDifferences.name: gettype.name
knownDifferences.difference: No reflection: GetType() is not available in JavaScript.
knownDifferences.alternative: Use nameof for names, pattern matching (`is`) for type tests, or WebSharper.JavaScript.Object.GetPrototypeOf for the JavaScript prototype.

knownDifferences.name: span.sum
knownDifferences.code: { Span<int> s = stackalloc int[] { 1, 2, 3 }; var t = 0; foreach (var x in s) t += x; return $"{t}"; }
knownDifferences.difference: Span<T> and stackalloc are not supported.
knownDifferences.alternative: Use arrays, or JavaScript typed arrays from WebSharper.JavaScript.

knownDifferences.name: datetime.iso
knownDifferences.difference: A DateTime has no Kind in JavaScript: the "o" format writes local time with its offset, never "Z".
knownDifferences.alternative: Use DateTimeOffset, or Date.toISOString from WebSharper.JavaScript for a UTC timestamp.

knownDifferences.name: readonly.wrapper
knownDifferences.code: { var l = new List<int> { 1 }; var r = l.AsReadOnly(); l.Add(2); return $"{r.Count}"; }
knownDifferences.difference: AsReadOnly returns a snapshot, not a live wrapper: it doesn't see later changes to the list.
knownDifferences.alternative: Call AsReadOnly again after changing the list, or pass the list as IReadOnlyList<T>.

knownDifferences.name: sorteddictionary.keys.live
knownDifferences.code: { var d = new SortedDictionary<int, string> { [1] = "a" }; var keys = d.Keys; d[2] = "b"; return $"{keys.Count}"; }
knownDifferences.difference: SortedDictionary.Keys and .Values are snapshots, not live views: they don't see later changes.
knownDifferences.alternative: Read Keys/Values again after changing the dictionary.

knownDifferences.name: typeof.name
knownDifferences.difference: No reflection: System.Type is not available in JavaScript, and a partial typeof(T).Name would suggest otherwise.
knownDifferences.alternative: Use nameof(T) for names, or WebSharper.JavaScript.Object.GetPrototypeOf for the JavaScript prototype.

knownDifferences.name: typeof.fullname
knownDifferences.difference: No reflection: System.Type is not available in JavaScript, and a partial typeof(T).Name would suggest otherwise.
knownDifferences.alternative: Use nameof(T) for names, or WebSharper.JavaScript.Object.GetPrototypeOf for the JavaScript prototype.
